items.title: Breaking: Headline inflation eases to 4.2 per cent in April as fuel prices fall
items.description: Headline inflation decelerated in April, with consumer prices increasing at an annual pace of 4.2 per cent, down from 4.6 per cent in March.

items.title: Media leaks ahead of Ben Roberts-Smith arrest referred to corruption commission
items.description: News crews were at Sydney Airport as a plane carrying Ben Roberts-Smith landed, and captured images of his arrest from inside the terminal.

items.title: Koalas at risk of death once seven-day temps rise beyond 27C
items.description: The risks of death or hospitalisation of koalas increases as soon as seven-day average maximum temperature is above 27 degrees Celsius, a new study shows.

items.title: Overhaul could affect how more than 1 million Australians access JobSeeker
items.description: Jobseeker services will shift away from a one-size-fits-all approach to a new tiered model, to be unveiled by the government later today.

items.title: Live: Odds of June rate hike close to zero after inflation fall
items.description: Today's inflation announcement reveals rates have eased to below what was expected, suggesting the Reserve Bank may not raise cash rates next month. Follow live.

items.title: Iran calls U.S. strikes a ceasefire breach as Qatar talks continue
items.description: The U.S. military launched strikes against missile installations and vessels in southern Iran on Monday, targeting sites near Bandar Abbas along the Strait of Hormuz, in a move that drew immediate condemnation from Tehran and threatened to upend fragile peace negotiations taking place simultaneously in Qatar.

items.title: Iran calls latest US strikes 'bad faith' sign as internet slowly restored
items.description: Iran has denounced US strikes in the country's south as a sign of "bad faith and unreliability" as negotiations toward a possible deal to end the war continue.

items.title: Fidel Castro's daughter fled his regime, and has a warning for the US
items.description: Fidel Castro's daughter says the US has failed to find a way to deal with Cuba for decades. But she tells the ABC that the Trump administration has a difference that could spell the end of the regime she fled.

items.title: Why drones fell from the sky during Sydney's Vivid light show
items.description: The company behind the drone shows at Sydney's Vivid festival said spectators were not at risk when almost 90 unmanned aircraft fell from the sky during a display on Monday night.

items.title: The BHP files reveal a big problem facing the mining giant
items.description: For a company that prides itself on digging out the metals for the world's clean energy future, saying nothing about its own clean energy future is not an option.

items.title: Israel intensifies Lebanon strikes as US-Iran deal nears

featured_image.name: Israel will escalate strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon, Netanyahu says |  Reuters

items.description: Israel is pressing the United States to guarantee its continued freedom to conduct military operations in Lebanon as part of any emerging peace framework with Iran, even as Israeli airstrikes killed multiple people in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley on Tuesday and the country's opposition leader declared the prospective agreement a failure.

items.title: Australian students record worst tech literacy results on record
items.description: Australian students have recorded their worst-ever results in national tests that measure digital literacy, with just 37 per cent of year 10 students and 50 per cent of year 6 students assessed as proficient.

items.title: Iran's judiciary blocks presidential order to restore internet

featured_image.name: Iran judiciary suspends presidential body after it ordered internet restored  | The Straits Times

items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the restoration of international internet access on May 25, seeking to end what has become the longest nationwide internet shutdown in history. Internet monitoring group NetBlocks confirmed partial connectivity was restored on Tuesday. But within hours, Iran's judiciary suspended the very presidential body responsible for carrying out the order, plunging the country's digital future into uncertainty.

items.title: BP removes chairman Albert Manifold over conduct concerns
items.description: BP on Tuesday removed Albert Manifold as chairman and director with immediate effect, citing "serious concerns" related to governance standards, oversight, and conduct — a sudden ouster that came just eight months into his tenure atop the British oil giant.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran warns of strikes 'beyond regional borders' after US hits southern Iran

featured_image.name: Iran Threatens to Strike Beyond the Middle East if the U.S. Resumes Attacks  - The New York Times

items.description: Iran's armed forces issued sharp warnings on Tuesday, May 26, threatening an expanded and more devastating military response if the United States and Israel resume strikes, after Washington carried out what it described as "self-defense strikes" in southern Iran near the Strait of Hormuz over the preceding 48 hours.

items.title: Zelensky says US missile defense talks have stalled

featured_image.name: Zelensky Says Kyiv Preparing Talks on Joint EU Air Shield, Warns of  'Russian World' Risk

items.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that strengthening Ukraine's air defense is Kyiv's "first priority" and disclosed that talks with the United States on expanding anti-ballistic missile production have stalled, pushing Ukraine to accelerate its own efforts in Europe.

items.title: Cuba publishes names of 2,000 pardoned prisoners

featured_image.name: Cuba pardons more than 2,000 prisoners amid US pressure

items.description: Cuba on Monday disclosed the identities of more than 2,000 prisoners pardoned under a sweeping amnesty first announced in April, publishing their names in the country's official government gazette for the first time since the decree was signed nearly two months ago.

items.title: Putin signs decree canceling debts for new Ukraine war recruits

featured_image.name: Russia's Putin provides debt relief to new Ukraine war recruits and ...

items.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Monday canceling debts of up to 10 million roubles — roughly $140,000 — for new military recruits and their spouses, the Kremlin announced, as Moscow continues to deploy financial incentives to sustain its war effort in Ukraine more than four years after the full-scale invasion began.

items.title: US strikes Iranian targets near Hormuz amid fragile peace talks

featured_image.name: US forces conduct 'self-defense' strikes in Iran, CENTCOM says

items.description: The U.S. military launched strikes targeting Iranian missile launch sites and boats near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, describing the action as "self-defense" even as fragile peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran continue.

items.title: Iran says Khamenei suffered only 'superficial' wounds in February airstrikes

featured_image.name: Iran says Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei suffered only minor injuries ...

items.description: Iran's Health Ministry on Monday publicly detailed for the first time the injuries sustained by Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei during the February 28 US-Israeli strikes on Tehran, describing them as minor and dismissing months of international reports that he had been critically wounded or disfigured.

items.title: President Trump Announces U.S. Military Airstrike in Venezuela
items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.title: Trump Meets Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago for Gaza Ceasefire Phase Two Talks
items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.title: Feds Launch Massive Taxpayer Fraud Probe in Minnesota After Viral Video
items.description: Federal agencies including DHS, FBI, and ICE investigate $110 million in suspected fraud at Minnesota child care centers following a viral YouTube video[3].

items.title: Americans Express Widespread Opposition to AI Data Centers
items.description: Public backlash against AI infrastructure data centers grows, with protests and demands for bans influencing Democratic Party strategies for future elections[3].

items.title: Elon Musk's Humanoid Robot Vision: China Poised to Lead Production
items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].

items.title: Trump-Putin Call Amid Ukraine-Russia Tensions Over Peace Plan
items.description: President Trump spoke with Putin amid ongoing Ukraine conflict, with Russia reevaluating peace plan tenets after Ukrainian denials[1].

items.title: Democratic Gubernatorial Candidates in Wisconsin Focus on Inflation and Trump
items.description: Seven Democrats vying for Wisconsin governor blame economic issues on Trump and emphasize affordability ahead of 2026 primary[3].
